correctness.rationale: The density has uniform margins; nonnegativity everywhere is necessary by continuity (a negative boundary point gives interior negativity) and sufficient by integration. At fixed z=|cos(2πu)cos(2πv)| the least linear contribution is -2|a|z. If s,t are the absolute cosines, s²+t² ranges between 2z and 1+z² with the endpoints realized by (sqrt(z),sqrt(z)) and (1,z). For b<0 the reduced concave quadratic has smaller endpoint value 1+2b-2|a|; b=0 is linear. For b>0 the reduced quadratic is 1-2b-2|a|z+4bz². Its minimizing z is min(1,|a|/(4b)), and z=0 excludes b>1/2 outright. The endpoint-to-vertex transition on the validity boundary is at 1+2b=8b, giving b=1/6. Both signed concordances vanish independently by invariance under reflection of just one margin, which reverses their signs. Integrating the squared conditional-CDF deviation gives 6 times a²/(4π²)+b²/(16π²), with no cross term by cosine orthogonality. On the first positivity branch the resulting bracket a²+b²/4 has maximum 65/144 by endpoint comparison; on the curved branch it is 16/31-(31/4)(b-8/31)². Thus the stated two signed maximizers are exhaustive. Expanding centered functions in the two normalized cosine modes gives Cov(f,g)=a f1 g1+b f2 g2, so maximal absolute correlation is max(|a|,|b|); the curved boundary satisfies |a|²<=1/2-8(b-1/4)², while the other branch and |b| cannot reach 1/sqrt(2). These are two-mode, population results, with boundary zeros allowed. Replay: RESULT.md lines 39–74; the uploaded symbolic check was inspected, not executed.
